events.title: Leonardo da Vinci is born
events.description: The future painter, inventor and scientist was born in the Tuscan town of Vinci, near Florence, the illegitimate son of a notary and a local peasant woman.
events.significance: Leonardo became the archetype of the Renaissance polymath. His works, including the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper, and his notebooks full of inventions still shape art and science today.

events.title: Abraham Lincoln dies after being shot
events.description: President Abraham Lincoln died at 7:22 a.m. in the Petersen House, across from Ford's Theatre in Washington, D.C. He had been shot by John Wilkes Booth the night before.
events.significance: Lincoln was the first U.S. president to be assassinated. His death came days after the Civil War effectively ended, and it reshaped the nation's course during Reconstruction.

events.title: The Titanic sinks
events.description: At about 2:20 a.m., the British ocean liner Titanic slipped beneath the North Atlantic. It had struck an iceberg shortly before midnight on April 14, on its maiden voyage.
events.significance: The sinking killed more than 1,500 people. It exposed the dangers of overconfidence in technology and led to major reforms in maritime safety, including lifeboat requirements and round-the-clock radio watches.

events.title: Jackie Robinson debuts for the Brooklyn Dodgers
events.description: Jackie Robinson took the field at first base at Ebbets Field. He became the first Black player in the modern major leagues.
events.significance: His debut broke baseball's color barrier and became a landmark moment in the American civil rights movement. His career inspired lasting change in sport and society.

events.title: Fire engulfs Notre-Dame Cathedral
events.description: A blaze broke out under the roof of Paris's famed Notre-Dame Cathedral on the evening of April 15. It destroyed the spire and much of the roof as crowds watched around the world.
events.significance: The fire shocked the world and set off a global outpouring of donations. It also started a major restoration effort to save one of the great landmarks of medieval Europe.
